name: Neariah
overview: Neariah was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Shecaniah. His lineage is noted in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 3:22, situating him within the royal family line. Beyond his paternal connection, no additional personal details or notable events are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Neariah means "[young] man of y-h-v-h," reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD (Yahweh). This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:22, though not explicitly given by God, reveals a cultural emphasis on divine association in naming.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Neariah was the son of Shecaniah. Additionally, it is inferred from subsequent genealogical listings in 1 Chronicles 3:23 that Neariah was the father of Shemaiah, Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam. These relationships place Neariah within a multi-generational family line of Judah.
scriptureSignificance: Neariah's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of Judah's royal lineage, as preserved in 1 Chronicles 3. His mention helps maintain the continuity of the Davidic line, which is foundational for understanding God's covenant promises concerning the Messiah. Though not prominent individually, Neariah's role as a link in this lineage underscores the faithfulness of God's providential plan through generations.
